data.name: Dharanipal
data.gender_notes: Dharanipal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words 'dharana' meaning 'to hold' and 'pal' meaning 'earth'. Dharanipal is the name of a divine being believed to hold the earth in Hindu mythology. The name Dharanipal carries the meaning “Holder of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharanipal usually hope their child will grow to embody holder of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes stability, protection, and the connection between the divine and the natural world.
data.etymology: Dharanipal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Holder of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharanipal total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Dharanipal is a name deeply rooted in Hindu culture and mythology. In Hindu mythology, various gods and goddesses are believed to hold the Earth on their shoulders or through their energies. Among these deities, Dharanipal, also known as Sthaanavaasah, holds a significant place. He is believed to support the Earth and prevent it from tilting, thus maintaining balance. Narratives of the gods often depict Dharanipal holding Mount Meru, the sacred mountain in Hinduism, on his head and upholding the cosmos.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dharanipal holds a profound spiritual significance in Hinduism. It signifies the divine power and strength that upholds the universe. It symbolizes the belief in the interconnectedness and balance of all things and the role each entity plays in maintaining that delicate balance. The name serves as a reminder of the importance of steadfastness, commitment, and the power of holding things close to the heart. The spiritual journey for one who carries this name can be a reminder to provide stability, support, and be the foundation for others and for the world around them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dharani: Symbol of stability and protection. Pal: Protector or guardian. Thus, Dharanipal signifies one who provides stability and protection.

vedic_reference.note: Dharanipal is a Vedic name mentioned in the Rigveda and other ancient Indian texts as a deity associated with the earth and fertility.

historical_references.reference: According to the Puranas, King Dharanipal was a ruler of the Vatsa kingdom in ancient India. He is said to have ruled during the late 6th century BC. During his reign, he was known for his extreme generosity and kindness towards his subjects.

Another reference to Dharanipal comes from the Jataka tales, a collection of Buddhist stories. In one tale, Dharanipal is described as a just and generous king who ruled over Magadha during the 5th century BC. He is renowned for his kindness towards animals and is said to have built a park for the protection of animals.
